I'm a DevOps engineer at ALGOcas and a fourth-year AI student at Menofia University. I build and automate AWS infrastructure, and I don't call a project done until I've seen it work. The backup project below ends with a restore in a second region, not just a completed backup job.

## What I've built

<img src="assets/projects.svg" width="100%" alt="Architecture flows of the three projects below">

- [aws-backup-disaster-recovery](https://github.com/mohamed-ibrahim09/aws-backup-disaster-recovery): Backs up an EC2 web server into a KMS-encrypted vault with Vault Lock, copies it to another region, and restores it there. The restored site returned HTTP 200 and the data file was intact.
- [AWS-Agentic-Travel-Assistant](https://github.com/mohamed-ibrahim09/AWS-Agentic-Travel-Assistant): A travel agent on Lambda and Bedrock that answers from a knowledge base, keeps session memory in S3, and calls tools over MCP. API Gateway and Cognito sit in front, and X-Ray traces each request.
- [AWS-Cloud-Infrastructure-Dashboard](https://github.com/mohamed-ibrahim09/AWS-Cloud-Infrastructure-Dashboard): A React and FastAPI app on EC2 behind an Application Load Balancer and an Auto Scaling group across two Availability Zones, with CloudWatch logs and metrics.

I hold the AWS Solutions Architect Associate (SAA-C03) and CCNA certifications, and took part in the DEPI DevOps program and GCI World 2026 (Matsuo-Iwasawa Lab, University of Tokyo).
